model_organism.citation: Mitofusin-2 Regulates Platelet Mitochondria and Function (PMID: 38156445)
phenotypes: Megakaryocyte/platelet-specific Mfn2 deletion (Pf4-Cre) caused fragmented mitochondria in megakaryocytes
Reduced platelet counts and shortened platelet life span
Increased phosphatidylserine exposure in resting platelets, especially aged platelets
Reduced activated oxygen consumption rate, ROS generation, calcium flux, and platelet-neutrophil aggregate formation
Decreased ischemic stroke infarct size after cerebral ischemia-reperfusion
Exacerbated pulmonary inflammatory hemorrhage after LPS-induced acute lung injury

phenotypes: Homozygotes have low birth weight and die within a day of birth

Heterozygous and homozygous MEFs show fragmented mitochondria
Homozygous tissues show decreased mitochondrial DNA and ATP

biological.citation: Hu et al. 2020 - The AMPK-MFN2 axis regulates MAM dynamics and autophagy induced by energy stresses (PMID: 32249716)
biological.summary: AMPK translocates to the MAM and mitochondria under energy stress and interacts directly with MFN2. Mfn2-/- MEFs have fewer MAMs, attenuated energy-stress-induced autophagy, and reduced oxygen consumption and glycolysis (not seen with MFN1 loss). Re-expressing MFN2 rescues the autophagy defect.

biological.citation: Mitofusin-2 Regulates Platelet Mitochondria and Function (PMID: 38156445)
biological.summary: The MFN2 SNP rs1474868 T allele (T/T) is associated with reduced platelet MFN2 RNA and protein, lower platelet counts, fragmented megakaryocyte mitochondria and reduced mitochondrial membrane potential. Megakaryocyte/platelet-specific Mfn2 knockout mice have reduced platelet counts and life span, prolonged bleeding times, smaller stroke infarcts and worse lung-injury hemorrhage. MFN2 SNPs were also associated with 28-day ARDS mortality in the iSPAAR study.
biological.sample_size: Human genotyped platelet donors, Pf4-Cre Mfn2 cKO mice, iSPAAR ARDS cohort (sizes not given)
biological.significance: Significant association with ARDS 28-day mortality (p-value not given)

biological.citation: Hernández-Alvarez et al. 2019 - Deficient Endoplasmic Reticulum-Mitochondrial Phosphatidylserine Transfer Causes Liver Disease (PMID: 31051106)
biological.summary: MFN2 binds phosphatidylserine and extracts it into membrane domains, promoting PS transfer to mitochondria and mitochondrial PE synthesis. Hepatic Mfn2 is reduced in NASH patients and mouse models. Liver-specific Mfn2 ablation causes ER stress, steatosis, inflammation, fibrosis and liver cancer, and re-expression ameliorates NASH in mice.

biological.citation: Mourier et al. 2015 - Mitofusin 2 is required to maintain mitochondrial coenzyme Q levels (PMID: 25688136)
biological.summary: Loss of MFN2 impairs respiration and ATP production by depleting the mitochondrial coenzyme Q pool, through a role in the terpenoid biosynthesis pathway. CoQ10 supplementation partially rescues the respiratory defect.

biological.citation: Chen et al. 2007 - Mitochondrial fusion protects against neurodegeneration in the cerebellum (PMID: 17693261)
biological.summary: Cerebellum-specific Mfn2 deletion in mice shows that Purkinje cells need Mfn2, but not Mfn1, for dendritic outgrowth, spine formation and survival. Mutant cells have abnormal mitochondrial distribution, ultrastructure and electron transport chain activity. Fibroblasts lacking fusion have mitochondria without mtDNA nucleoids. This is a model for CMT2A neurodegeneration.

biological.citation: Mitochondria-ER contact mediated by MFN2-SERCA2 interaction supports CD8+ T cell metabolic fitness and function in tumors (PMID: 37738362)
biological.summary: MFN2 interacts with ER Ca2+-ATPase SERCA2 to enhance mitochondria-ER contacts and stimulate SERCA2 Ca2+ retrieval, which supports mitochondrial Ca2+ influx and prevents excessive Ca2+ accumulation and apoptosis. Mfn2 deletion in CD8+ T cells impairs metabolism and promotes tumor growth. MFN2 expression correlates positively with prognosis across multiple cancers.

biological.citation: Mfn2 Regulates High Glucose-Induced MAMs Dysfunction and Apoptosis in Podocytes via PERK Pathway (PMID: 34988075)
biological.summary: Mfn2 is suppressed in glomeruli and podocytes of DKD patients and STZ-diabetic rats. Mfn2 physically interacts with PERK, and high glucose reduces this interaction. Mfn2 knockdown causes MAM loss, mitochondrial dysfunction, PERK activation and apoptosis, while Mfn2 overexpression reverses these effects.

biological.citation: MFN2 coordinates mitochondria motility with α-tubulin acetylation and this regulation is disrupted in CMT2A (PMID: 38883841)
biological.summary: MFN2 recruits α-tubulin acetyltransferase ATAT1 to mitochondria-microtubule contacts, driving local α-tubulin acetylation that regulates mitochondrial transport. CMT2A mutations R94W and T105M may impair ATAT1 release at these sites.

biological.citation: Mfn2 inhibits proliferation and cell-cycle in Hela cells via Ras-NF-κB signal pathway (PMID: 31384172)
biological.summary: Mfn2 overexpression in HeLa cells, localized to the cytoplasm, reduces PCNA and Cyclin D1, causes G0/G1 arrest, and decreases Ras pathway proteins (Myc, NF-κB p65, STAT3). It also inhibits tumor growth in a xenograft model.

biological.citation: Regulatory roles of external cholesterol in human airway epithelial mitochondrial function through STARD3 signalling (PMID: 35678098)
biological.summary: External cholesterol acts through a STARD3-MFN2 pathway to alter mitochondrial function and dynamics in airway epithelial cells exposed to cigarette smoke extract. MFN2 down-regulation increases IL production, partly by impairing fatty acid oxidation and activating mTOR phosphorylation.
